findings.why: 44 asserts in these ten headers fire with no message, so a failed PopFront prints only a file and line, and the reader cannot tell empty-from-uninitialized from emptied.
findings.fix: Give every bounds and empty assert a one-clause message, as RingQueue's "RingQueue is full" already does; the module already carries the pattern.

findings.why: Placement new appears 26 times across six of these headers, no file in Engine/Container includes <new>, and a probe that includes only Vector.h still compiles - so the declaration is arriving transitively from libc++ rather than from anything the file declares.
findings.fix: Add #include <new> to Vector.h, Deque.h, Array.h, Map.h, HashMap.h and RingQueue.h, which are the six that use it.

findings.why: Array.h constructs and destroys elements in place and names neither <new> nor anything that promises it.
Queue.h names no size_t, no nullptr_t and no std::nullptr_t; the header's whole vocabulary is Deque, FatalAssert and std::move.
findings.fix: Delete the include and let the build gate confirm it.

findings.why: Array.h calls allocator.allocate and allocator.deallocate, which DefaultAllocator.h defines; the New/Delete helpers Memory.h names appear nowhere in the file.
findings.fix: Delete the include, or use New<> and Delete<> the way LinkedList.h does, which is the house idiom for an allocator-constructed object.

findings.why: The three nested iterators a module hands out are the classes a caller is most likely to derive from by accident, and none is sealed.
findings.fix: Mark Iterator and ConstIterator final; the module's own Pair and LinkedListNode already are.

findings.why: HashMap::Iterator and HashMap::ConstIterator are both inheritable, and both reach callers through Find and begin.
LinkedList::Iterator is the fourth unsealed iterator; 30 of the engine's 61 TestCollection subclasses already carry final, so sealing is the house position, not a new rule.
None of the module's ten test fixtures is final, so the one class that can never be a base is declared as if it could.
findings.fix: Add final to all ten; Core's TaskRegistryTest and ResultPacketTest are the model.

findings.why: InsertSorted default-constructs a TValue and Insert then assigns into it, so TValue must be default-constructible and assignable while nothing says so and a caller learns it from a template error at a distance.
findings.fix: static_assert(std::is_default_constructible_v<TValue> && std::is_assignable_v<TValue&, const TValue&>) on the class, and write the requirement on the class page.

findings.why: Resize is the one growth path that requires TElement to be default-constructible; every other path takes a value, so the requirement arrives only when someone calls Resize.
findings.fix: static_assert(std::is_default_constructible_v<TElement>) beside the class, or take a fill value in Resize's signature.

findings.why: The parameter ptr names the member it initialises, which is the collision the in prefix exists to remove; the same shape is in all four nested iterators.
findings.fix: Rename to inPtr here, inNode in LinkedList.h, and inMap and inIndex in HashMap.h.

findings.evidence: explicit Iterator(TMap* map, TIndex index) noexcept
findings.why: Both parameters name the members they initialise, so the initializer list reads map(map), index(index) in two of the module's iterators.
findings.fix: Rename to inMap and inIndex in Iterator and ConstIterator.

findings.why: node(node) again, and this iterator is the one the module's own range-for depends on.
Array::Swap takes an rvalue while Deque, Vector, RingQueue and Map take an lvalue reference, so a.Swap(b) does not compile and Clear() has to construct a temporary to express the same thing.
findings.fix: Take Array& like its four siblings, and let Clear() pass a named empty Array.

findings.why: Remove asserts the address-identity precondition and then calls GetNodeOf, which asserts the identical thing again; two copies of one contract is two places to update.
findings.fix: Keep the assert in GetNodeOf, where the cast lives, and drop the one in Remove.

findings.why: Reserve is the only public mutator in the class without noexcept, and the Rehash it calls is marked; the omission is invisible to a caller choosing between Reserve and Grow.
findings.fix: Mark it noexcept, matching the rest of the file.
